requirements.quote: DUP flag In this example the DUP flag is set to zero (0) to indicate that the message is being sent for the first time.
requirements.condition: When the message is sent for the first time.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Setting the DUP flag to 1 on the first transmission.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the DUP flag of an initial transmission.

requirements.quote: If this message is being re-sent because a SUBACK message has not arrived after a specified timeout period, the DUP bit is set to indicate to the broker that it might be a duplicate of a message already received.
requirements.condition: When retransmitting because a SUBACK has not arrived within the specified timeout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retransmitting with the DUP bit clear.
requirements.why_checkable: A timeout test can inspect the DUP bit on the resulting retransmission.

requirements.quote: RETAIN flag Not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the RETAIN flag to convey protocol semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be checked for whether it assigns or depends on RETAIN semantics for this message.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length This is the length of the Payload.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the described UNSUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or interpret Remaining Length as the payload length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Remaining Length that differs from the payload length.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Remaining Length can be compared directly with the payload byte count.

requirements.quote: It can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When the Remaining Length requires a multibyte representation.
requirements.required_behavior: Support a multibyte Remaining Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Restricting this Remaining Length field to one byte.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can use a payload whose length requires multiple Remaining Length bytes.

requirements.quote: Variable header The variable header contains a Message ID because an UNSUBSCRIBE message has a QoS level of 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Message ID in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting the Message ID from the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized variable header can be inspected for the Message ID field.

requirements.quote: Message ID 0 (0x0000) is reserved as an invalid Message ID, and must not be used.
requirements.condition: When assigning or encoding a Message ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using Message ID 0 (0x0000).
requirements.why_checkable: Generated and serialized Message IDs can be checked for the reserved zero value.

requirements.quote: The Message ID is a 16-bit unsigned integer, which typically increases by exactly one from one message to the next, but is not required to do so.
requirements.condition: When representing or encoding a Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Message ID as a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding the Message ID outside the unsigned 16-bit representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and decoded numeric range are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: The two bytes of the Message ID are ordered as MSB, followed by LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Order the bytes as MSB followed by LSB.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding the Message ID in little-endian byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: A Message ID with unequal bytes can verify byte order.

requirements.quote: Payload The client unsubscribes from the list of topics named in the payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the payload entries as the list of topics from which the client unsubscribes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Unsubscribing from topics not named in the payload solely due to this message.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker subscription state can be compared with the topics encoded in the payload.

requirements.quote: The strings are UTF-encoded and are packed contiguously.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding topic strings in an UNSUBSCRIBE payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode each topic string using the specified UTF encoding.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a non-UTF representation for the topic strings.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload bytes can be decoded and checked against UTF encoding rules.

requirements.quote: The strings are UTF-encoded and are packed contiguously.
requirements.condition: When encoding multiple topic strings in an UNSUBSCRIBE payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Inserting unspecified gaps or padding between the encoded strings.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload layout can be inspected for padding between successive strings.

requirements.quote: Topic names in a UNSUBSCRIBE message are not compressed.
requirements.condition: When encoding topic names in an UNSUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Compressing topic names.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized topic names can be checked for their complete uncompressed representation.

requirements.quote: Response The broker sends an UNSUBACK to a client in response to an UNSUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.condition: When the broker responds to an UNSUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Send an UNSUBACK to the client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a different acknowledgment message as the UNSUBSCRIBE response.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker can be sent an UNSUBSCRIBE and its response packet type inspected.

requirements.quote: The UNSUBACK message is sent by the broker to the client to confirm receipt of an UNSUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: Send it from the broker to the client as confirmation of receipt of an UNSUBSCRIBE.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending UNSUBACK in the opposite direction or without the stated acknowledgment role.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet direction and the triggering UNSUBSCRIBE can be observed in a protocol trace.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (11) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 1 0 1 1 x x x x
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding another Message Type value.
requirements.why_checkable: The high four bits of the first fixed-header byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining length (2) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding an UNSUBACK Remaining Length other than 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The Remaining Length field is directly observable in the packet.

requirements.quote: QoS level Not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the QoS field to convey UNSUBACK semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for whether UNSUBACK behavior depends on this field.

requirements.quote: DUP flag Not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the DUP flag to convey UNSUBACK semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for whether UNSUBACK behavior depends on this flag.

requirements.quote: RETAIN flag Not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the RETAIN flag to convey UNSUBACK semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for whether UNSUBACK behavior depends on this flag.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length The length of the Variable Header (2 bytes).
requirements.required_behavior: Make Remaining Length equal to the two-byte variable-header length.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including any length beyond the two-byte variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The field value can be compared with the encoded variable-header size.

requirements.quote: Variable header The variable header contains the Message ID for the UNSUBSCRIBE message that is being acknowledged.
requirements.condition: When constructing or processing an UNSUBACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Message ID of the acknowledged UNSUBSCRIBE in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using a Message ID that does not identify the acknowledged UNSUBSCRIBE.
requirements.why_checkable: The UNSUBACK Message ID can be compared with the triggering UNSUBSCRIBE Message ID.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message ID MSB byte 2 Message ID LSB
requirements.condition: When encoding an UNSUBACK variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Message ID MSB first and LSB second.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reversing the Message ID byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: The order of the two variable-header bytes is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet length and bytes after the variable header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The PINGREQ message is an "are you alive" message that is sent from or received by a connected client.
requirements.condition: When a client sends or receives PINGREQ.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating PINGREQ as a message for a client outside the connected state.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can correlate PINGREQ processing with the client connection state.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (12) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 1 1 0 0 x x x x
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding another Message Type value.
requirements.why_checkable: The high four bits of the first fixed-header byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (0) 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a nonzero Remaining Length.
requirements.why_checkable: The Remaining Length field is directly observable.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the DUP flag to convey PINGREQ semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGREQ DUP flag.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the QoS field to convey PINGREQ semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGREQ QoS field.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the RETAIN flag to convey PINGREQ semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGREQ RETAIN flag.

requirements.quote: Variable header There is no variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including a variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The PINGREQ packet layout can be inspected for bytes after its fixed header.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The PINGREQ packet length can be checked for absence of payload bytes.

requirements.quote: Response The response to a PINGREQ message is a PINGRESP message.
requirements.condition: When responding to a PINGREQ message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using another packet type as the PINGREQ response.
requirements.why_checkable: A PINGREQ can be sent and the resulting response packet type observed.

requirements.quote: A PINGRESP message is the response to a PINGREQ message and means "yes I am alive".
requirements.required_behavior: Use it as the response to a PINGREQ.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treating PINGRESP as an unrelated request message.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol trace can correlate each PINGRESP with its response role.

requirements.quote: Keep Alive messages flow in either direction, sent either by a connected client or the broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow Keep Alive messages to originate from either a connected client or the broker.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Restricting Keep Alive messages to only one direction.
requirements.why_checkable: Bidirectional Keep Alive behavior can be exercised with client-originated and broker-originated messages.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (13) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 1 1 0 1 x x x x
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding another Message Type value.
requirements.why_checkable: The high four bits of the first fixed-header byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (0) 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a nonzero Remaining Length.
requirements.why_checkable: The Remaining Length field is directly observable.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the DUP flag to convey PINGRESP semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGRESP DUP flag.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the QoS field to convey PINGRESP semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGRESP QoS field.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the RETAIN flag to convey PINGRESP semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the PINGRESP RETAIN flag.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The PINGRESP packet length can be checked for absence of payload bytes.

requirements.quote: Variable header There is no variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including a variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The PINGRESP packet layout can be inspected for bytes after its fixed header.

requirements.quote: The DISCONNECT message is sent from the client to the broker to indicate that it is about to close its TCP/IP connection.
requirements.condition: When a client is about to close its TCP/IP connection cleanly.
requirements.required_behavior: Send DISCONNECT from the client to the broker before closing.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending DISCONNECT from the broker to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet direction and its ordering before connection closure can be observed.

requirements.quote: Sending the DISCONNECT message does not affect existing subscriptions.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave existing subscriptions unaffected by that act alone.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Deleting subscriptions solely because DISCONNECT was sent.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscription state can be compared before and after DISCONNECT.

requirements.quote: They are persistent until they either explicitly unsubscribed, or if there is a clean start.
requirements.condition: After DISCONNECT, while neither explicit unsubscription nor a clean start has occurred.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Removing subscriptions before either stated terminating event.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnect tests can inspect persistence before and after the two stated events.

requirements.quote: The broker retains QoS 1 and QoS 1 messages for topics to which the client is unsubscribed until the client reconnects.
requirements.why_checkable: The duplicated QoS level and the statement that retention applies to topics from which the client is unsubscribed make the constrained message set unclear.

requirements.quote: QoS 0 messages are not retained, since they are delivered on a best efforts basis.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retaining QoS 0 messages for later delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: A disconnect-and-reconnect test can determine whether QoS 0 messages were retained.

requirements.quote: byte 1 Message Type (14) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 1 1 1 0 x x x x
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding another Message Type value.
requirements.why_checkable: The high four bits of the first fixed-header byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: byte 2 Remaining Length (0) 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encoding a nonzero Remaining Length.
requirements.why_checkable: The Remaining Length field is directly observable.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used in the DISCONNECT message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the DUP flag to convey DISCONNECT semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the DISCONNECT DUP flag.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used in the DISCONNECT message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the QoS field to convey DISCONNECT semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the DISCONNECT QoS field.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used in the DISCONNECT message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using the RETAIN flag to convey DISCONNECT semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be checked for dependency on the DISCONNECT RETAIN flag.

requirements.quote: Payload There is no payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including payload bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The DISCONNECT packet length can be checked for absence of payload bytes.

requirements.quote: Variable header There is no variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Including a variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The DISCONNECT packet layout can be inspected for bytes after its fixed header.

requirements.quote: A response is not expected and no retry semantics are defined in the protocol.
requirements.condition: When delivering a message at QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Expecting a protocol response for the message.
requirements.why_checkable: A QoS 0 exchange can be checked for response-dependent sender behavior.

requirements.quote: A response is not expected and no retry semantics are defined in the protocol.
requirements.condition: When delivering a message at QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Applying protocol-defined retry behavior to the message.
requirements.why_checkable: Failure and timeout tests can determine whether the implementation retries QoS 0 messages.

requirements.quote: The message arrives at the broker either once or not at all.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver the message to the broker at most once.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Delivering the same QoS 0 message to the broker more than once through protocol retry semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker deliveries can be counted during failure and retransmission scenarios.

requirements.quote: The receipt of a message by the broker is acknowledged by a PUBACK message.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives a QoS level 1 message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leaving successful receipt unacknowledged or acknowledging it with another packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker can receive a QoS 1 message and its acknowledgment packet type be inspected.

requirements.quote: If there is an identified failure of either the communications link or the sending device, or the acknowledgement message is not received after a specified period of time, the sender resends the message with the DUP bit set in the message header.
requirements.condition: When a communications-link or sending-device failure is identified, or the acknowledgment is not received within the specified period.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Failing to resend after either stated condition.
requirements.why_checkable: Failure and acknowledgment-timeout tests can observe whether retransmission occurs.

requirements.quote: If there is an identified failure of either the communications link or the sending device, or the acknowledgement message is not received after a specified period of time, the sender resends the message with the DUP bit set in the message header.
requirements.condition: When resending after either stated failure condition or acknowledgment timeout.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP bit in the retransmitted message header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Resending with the DUP bit clear.
requirements.why_checkable: The retransmitted packet header can be inspected after inducing each trigger condition.

requirements.quote: The message arrives at the broker at least once.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the message arrives at the broker at least once.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Completing the QoS 1 delivery flow without any broker receipt.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker receipt can be observed under normal and failure-recovery scenarios.

requirements.quote: Both SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE messages use QoS level 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using another QoS level.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits of a serialized SUBSCRIBE fixed header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Both SUBSCRIBE and UNSUBSCRIBE messages use QoS level 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using another QoS level.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS bits of a serialized UNSUBSCRIBE fixed header can be inspected.

requirements.quote: A message with QoS level 1 has a Message ID in the message header.
requirements.condition: For any message with QoS level 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Message ID in the message header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omitting the Message ID.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized QoS 1 messages can be inspected for the Message ID field.
